name_reason: Follows convention fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=save). Accurately describes the function: persists battle-runtime char state back into the menu/template roster array at chapter end. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: At chapter end, persist each battle-runtime party member's state back into the menu/template (party roster) array, restoring HP/MP and clearing transient combat status.
logic_summary: For each runtime party member rt_idx in [0, data_fd2_battle_party_member_count): rt_char = &runtime_char_array[rt_idx] (0x50-byte stride). Inner loop over template entries tmpl_idx in [0, data_fd2_shared_menu_party_member_count): tmpl = menu_party_roster_buffer + tmpl_idx*0x50. When rt_char.char_id (+8) == tmpl.char_id (+8): if char_id==0 (索爾) and fd2_check_char_is_dead(rt_idx) is true, skip (continue) so battle-death does not propagate. Otherwise memmove the whole 0x50-byte struct rt_char->tmpl, memset tmpl+0x22..+0x27 (6 bytes status block) to 0, mask tmpl[+5] flags &= 1 (keep only dead-bit), if not dead (flags!=1) copy hp_max(+0x42)->hp_current(+0x40), always copy mp_max(+0x46)->mp_current(+0x44), then call fd2_recompute_runtime_char_total_stats(tmpl_idx) to re-derive aggregate stats. Begins with stack-probe __CHK(0x20).

returns.semantics: No return value; mutates the menu/template roster buffer in place.

notes: Disasm confirms runtime_char stride is 0x50: EBP*4 + EBP = *5, << 4 = *0x50 added to [0x53A45]; identical pattern for tmpl from [0x53BF7]. Source uses pointer arithmetic data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr + rt_idx with the global typed as runtime_char* (0x50 bytes, types.h), which is equivalent and correct. Source comment (save.c lines 14-30) already accurate, precise, and ASCII-clean -> kept (no Edit to save.c). Ghidra plate previously referred to the template base as 'map_terrain_buffer'; the live global at 0x53BF7 is data_fd2_shared_menu_party_roster_buffer_ptr, so the plate was stale -> updated the plate to say 'menu_party_roster_buffer' and added stride/base annotations, preserving all behavioral detail. writes_globals empty because the function mutates pointed-to buffer memory, not the global variables themselves. set_plate_comment 'missing Algorithm/Parameters/Returns section' warnings are cosmetic (freeform narrative plate style, consistent with codebase).
